@graph.headline: Home Builder Website Design, Proof, and Conversion
@graph.description: Plan a home builder website around buyer fit, project proof, clear process, accessible design, search foundations, conversion paths, ownership, and testing.

mainEntity.name: What should a home builder website include?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should include clear audience and market fit, approved project proof, people, process, buyer questions, qualification guidance, a useful next step, accessible design, reliable forms, and an owned maintenance plan.

mainEntity.name: Should a builder choose a template or custom website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose based on strategy, required modules, editing needs, ownership, accessibility, performance, integrations, maintenance, budget, and timeline. A template can work well when it meets those requirements.

mainEntity.name: How important is mobile design for a builder website?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is essential. Key images, proof, process, forms, links, and navigation must remain readable and usable on real phones, with acceptable loading and no horizontal overflow.

mainEntity.name: Does a beautiful website automatically generate leads?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Design can support trust and clarity, but discovery, audience fit, proof, conversion paths, follow-up, market conditions, and sales execution also affect outcomes.

mainEntity.name: Who should own a home builder website after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: The builder should know who owns the domain, hosting, platform access, content approvals, maintenance, security, analytics, forms, backups, and rollback process, even when specialists manage the work.
